cond_0001.intro:
The Clinical Strategy & Analytics (CS&A) Team at [Company name masked] is seeking a Lead Research Scientist.
Healthcare is rapidly changing, and our members are living longer, often with more chronic conditions. The Clinical Strategy & Analytics team identifies opportunities and builds solutions to improve clinical outcomes and lower costs for millions of Medicare Advantage beneficiaries through an evidence-based approach using data analytics, clinical expertise, strategic mindset, and rigorous study designs. In this multi-disciplinary team, you will have the opportunity to work closely with strategy partners and clinicians to shape [Company name masked]'s enterprise clinical strategies and initiatives.
The Lead Research Scientist will be involved in all aspects of analytics needed to support the launch and success of clinical intervention programs. This can include analytic tasks related to population health opportunity sizing, trend and financial alignment, study design, data engineering and operational support, marketing analysis support, clinical outcomes analysis, presentations/publications, and work management. A Lead Research Scientist is a senior member of Clinical Analytics and often independently represents the work and moves initiatives forward.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
As a Lead Research Scientist in this role, you will:
Be fluent working with large, complex medical claims data using analytics technologies (SQL, SAS, Python/Pyspark, Databricks, Microsoft Azure, PowerBI) and analytics methodologies (exploratory/descriptive analysis, predictive modeling, causal outcomes research, and data visualization). Deliver trusted analysis in a timely manner. This involves prioritizing and planning your work, setting realistic timelines for delivering analysis results, and communicating with business partners on the status of work. Have expertise on [Company name masked]'s business, clinical, and Rx performance measures and KPIs. This will involve collaboration with clinicians, clinical informaticists, and business partners to understand terminology, measurement, and coding specifications. Lead with the leveraging of analytics to help the business and clinical intervention programs be more successful. This involves you filling a variety of roles in a project that can range from data engineering/architecture, business intelligence, behavioral economics, machine learning, to analytics DevOps support. Build strong rapport with [Company name masked] decision-makers and business partners. This will involve keeping a great attitude working with others who are not as strong with analytics, being able to explain things well, and trying to serve the needs of decision-makers you work with. This role leads and supports strategic analytics for development and execution of BH Strategy and to support opportunity sizing and viability of multiple vendors brought forward by our Discovery and Strategic Partnership stakeholders.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Master's Degree in a quantitative discipline such as Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Economics, Statistics, Clinical Informatics, and/or related fields
Experience and comfort with manipulating and analyzing data using SQL plus another language such as SAS, Python/Pyspark, or R
6+ Years experience in analytics and/or quantitative research
Experience working with medical or pharmacy claims data
Preferred Requirements
Demonstrated knowledge of how to build predictive models from start to finish
Familiarity with clinical concepts related to a broad range of clinical conditions and disease states
Experience evaluating clinical interventions used to improve clinical outcomes
cond_0001.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

Build strong rapport with [Company name masked] decision-makers and business partners. This will involve maintaining a collaborative attitude when working with those who are less familiar with analytics, explaining things clearly, and helping to serve the needs of the people you work with.
Coordinate strategic analytics for the development and execution of BH Strategy and help assess opportunity sizing and viability of multiple vendors brought forward by Discovery and Strategic Partnership stakeholders.

Master's Degree in a quantitative discipline such as Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Economics, Statistics, Clinical Informatics, or related fields

Experience and comfort manipulating and analyzing data using SQL plus another language such as SAS, Python/Pyspark, or R

Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with clinical concepts related to a broad range of clinical conditions and disease states

cond_0100.intro:
The Clinical Strategy & Analytics (CS&A) team at [Company name masked] is seeking a Lead Research Scientist.
Healthcare is rapidly changing, and our members are living longer, often with more chronic conditions. The Clinical Strategy & Analytics team identifies opportunities and builds solutions to improve clinical outcomes and lower costs for millions of Medicare Advantage beneficiaries through an evidence-based approach using data analytics, clinical expertise, strategic mindset, and rigorous study designs. In this multi-disciplinary team, you will have the opportunity to work closely with strategy partners and clinicians to shape enterprise clinical strategies and initiatives.
The Lead Research Scientist will be involved in all aspects of analytics needed to support the launch and success of clinical intervention programs. This can include analytic tasks related to population health opportunity sizing, trend and financial alignment, study design, data engineering and operational support, marketing analysis support, clinical outcomes analysis, presentations/publications, and work management. A Lead Research Scientist is a senior member of Clinical Analytics and often independently represents the work and moves initiatives forward.
cond_0100.responsibilities:
As a Lead Research Scientist in this role, you will:
Be fluent working with large, complex medical claims data using analytics technologies (SQL, SAS, Python/Pyspark, Databricks, Microsoft Azure, PowerBI) and analytics methodologies (exploratory/descriptive analysis, predictive modeling, causal outcomes research, and data visualization). Deliver trusted analysis in a timely manner. This involves prioritizing and planning your work, setting realistic timelines for delivering analysis results, and communicating with business partners on the status of work. Have expertise on [Company name masked]'s business, clinical, and Rx performance measures and KPIs. This will involve collaboration with clinicians, clinical informaticists, and business partners to understand terminology, measurement, and coding specifications. Lead with the leveraging of analytics to help the business and clinical intervention programs be more successful. This involves filling a variety of roles in a project that can range from data engineering/architecture, business intelligence, behavioral economics, machine learning, to analytics DevOps support. Build strong rapport with [Company name masked] decision-makers and business partners. This will involve keeping a great attitude working with others who are not as strong with analytics, being able to explain things well, and trying to serve the needs of decision-makers you work with. This role leads and supports strategic analytics for development and execution of BH Strategy and to support opportunity sizing and viability of multiple vendors brought forward by our Discovery and Strategic Partnership stakeholders.

Master's Degree in a quantitative discipline such as Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Economics, Statistics, Clinical Informatics, and/or related fields
Experience and comfort with manipulating and analyzing data using SQL plus another language such as SAS, Python/Pyspark, or R.
Demonstrated knowledge of how to build predictive models from start to finish.
6+ Years experience in analytics and/or quantitative research
Experience working with medical or pharmacy claims data
Familiarity with clinical concepts related to a broad range of clinical conditions and disease states
Experience evaluating clinical interventions used to improve clinical outcomes

[Company name masked]'s Clinical Strategy and Analytics (CS&A) Team is seeking a Lead Research Scientist.
Healthcare is rapidly changing, and our members are living longer, often with more chronic conditions. The Clinical Strategy & Analytics team identifies opportunities and builds solutions to improve clinical outcomes and lower costs for millions of Medicare Advantage beneficiaries through an evidence-based approach using data analytics, clinical expertise, strategic mindset, and rigorous study designs. In this multi-disciplinary team, you will own close collaboration with strategy partners and clinicians to shape [Company name masked]'s enterprise clinical strategies and initiatives.
The Lead Research Scientist will take ownership of all aspects of analytics needed to support the launch and success of clinical intervention programs. This can include analytic tasks related to population health opportunity sizing, trend and financial alignment, study design, data engineering and operational support, marketing analysis support, clinical outcomes analysis, presentations/publications, and work management. A Lead Research Scientist is a senior member of Clinical Analytics and independently drives the work and moves initiatives forward.
cond_0224.responsibilities:

Direct fluent use of large, complex medical claims data using analytics technologies (SQL, SAS, Python/Pyspark, Databricks, Microsoft Azure, PowerBI) and analytics methodologies (exploratory/descriptive analysis, predictive modeling, causal outcomes research, and data visualization). Deliver trusted analysis in a timely manner. This involves prioritizing and planning your work, setting realistic timelines for delivering analysis results, and communicating with business partners on the status of work. Own expertise on [Company name masked]'s business, clinical, and Rx performance measures and KPIs. Lead the leveraging of analytics to make business and clinical intervention programs more successful. This involves filling a variety of roles in a project that can range from data engineering/architecture, business intelligence, behavioral economics, machine learning, to analytics DevOps support. Build strong rapport with [Company name masked] decision-makers and business partners. This will involve keeping a great attitude working with others who are not as strong with analytics, being able to explain things well, and serving the needs of decision-makers you work with. This role leads and drives strategic analytics for development and execution of BH Strategy and to support opportunity sizing and viability of multiple vendors brought forward by our Discovery and Strategic Partnership stakeholders.

cond_0333.intro:
[Company name masked]'s Clinical Strategy and Analytics (CS&A) Team is seeking a Lead Research Scientist.
Healthcare is rapidly changing, and our members are living longer, often with more chronic conditions. The Clinical Strategy & Analytics team identifies opportunities and builds solutions to improve clinical outcomes and lower costs for millions of Medicare Advantage beneficiaries through an evidence-based approach using data analytics, clinical expertise, strategic mindset, and rigorous study designs. In this multi-disciplinary team, you will have the opportunity to work closely with strategy partners and clinicians to shape [Company name masked]'s enterprise clinical strategies and initiatives.
The Lead Research Scientist will be involved in all aspects of analytics needed to support the launch and success of clinical intervention programs. This can include analytic tasks related to population health opportunity sizing, trend and financial alignment, study design, data engineering and operational support, marketing analysis support, clinical outcomes analysis, presentations/publications, and work management. A Lead Research Scientist is a senior member of Clinical Analytics and often represents the work collaboratively and helps move initiatives forward.
cond_0333.responsibilities:
As a Lead Research Scientist in this role, you will:
Work fluently with large, complex medical claims data using analytics technologies (SQL, SAS, Python/Pyspark, Databricks, Microsoft Azure, PowerBI) and analytics methodologies (exploratory/descriptive analysis, predictive modeling, causal outcomes research, and data visualization).
Deliver trusted analysis in a timely manner. This involves coordinating your work with business partners, setting realistic timelines, and keeping them informed on the status of deliverables.
Build shared understanding of [Company name masked]'s business, clinical, and Rx performance measures and KPIs. This will involve working alongside clinicians, clinical informaticists, and business partners to clarify terminology, measurement, and coding specifications.
Support the business and clinical intervention programs through analytics. This involves contributing across a variety of roles in a project, ranging from data engineering/architecture, business intelligence, behavioral economics, machine learning, to analytics DevOps support.
Build strong rapport with [Company name masked] decision-makers and business partners. This will involve maintaining a collaborative attitude when working with those who are less familiar with analytics, explaining things clearly, and helping to serve the needs of the people you work with.
Coordinate strategic analytics for the development and execution of BH Strategy and help assess opportunity sizing and viability of multiple vendors brought forward by Discovery and Strategic Partnership stakeholders.
cond_0333.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Master's Degree in a quantitative discipline such as Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Economics, Statistics, Clinical Informatics, or related fields
6+ Years of experience in analytics and/or quantitative research
Experience and comfort manipulating and analyzing data using SQL plus another language such as SAS, Python/Pyspark, or R
Demonstrated knowledge of how to build predictive models from start to finish
Experience working with medical or pharmacy claims data
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with clinical concepts related to a broad range of clinical conditions and disease states
Experience evaluating clinical interventions used to improve clinical outcomes
